notes: VERSION 2 (supersedes v1, 15dc51f -- see docs/gsl_methods_compare_2026-11-02_v2.md). Preliminary comparison of 6 published GSL methods (M1-M6) at the 15 'Figure GSL-IAV' sites. Two independent GPP series, never mixed within a method: nt = zero-floored GPP_NT_REF (no winter screen), dt = zero-floored GPP_DT_REF, each with its own P99/fine grid. M5/M6 use NEP only (variant='all'). Southern-Hemisphere (AU-How) uses Jul-Jun season years in EVERY method including M2-M4 and for P99, with a fresh day-count passing rule (<=14 failing days under the existing 0.25 daily-QC rule), not the v1 'both bracketing calendar years pass' proxy. M6 searches for start/end only within +/-30 days of M5-span's own start/end (k=3-9 day OLS slope on UNSMOOTHED NEP, median across k; no alternate-end). Two-season flag (M5-span/M6 only) uses the TIMESAT secondary-peak rule (Wang et al. 2020) on 15-day-smoothed NT GPP, not a slope-run rule. Checks (NH sites only, all passed exactly): NT-series M2@10%/M4@0.95 == derived_site_year.csv's main_unscreened gsl_z16/gsl_t95/f_z16/f_t95; every row has a value or an explanatory flag. See SESSION_LOG.md and the methods doc for AU-How's before/after comparison, DT-vs-NT partitioning uncertainty, and M6-vs-v1.
